title: Shofu Article Program: Little Smiles, Big Adventures
html:
Written by: Carter Bedinghaus, DMD

If you had told the little boy in this picture that one day he would be standing at graduation, receiving the Dean’s Award after four years of dental school, he probably would have smiled… and then asked, “What’s a dean?”

As I finished my final weeks at the LECOM School of Dental Medicine, I found myself reflecting on everything it had taken to reach that moment. When people asked why I kept getting emotional, my answer was simple: I loved every minute of dental school and was grateful for the journey that took me there.

One of the most unexpected experiences after graduation was filming an episode for a television show. I never imagined dentistry would lead me to a TV set, but it’s another reminder that this profession can take you places you never expect. Keep an eye out; you just might see me on your TV soon!

Shortly after celebrating graduation, it was time to begin my next chapter: pediatric dental residency.

Walking into residency brought back many of the same emotions I felt during my first days of dental school. There was excitement, anticipation, and, if I’m being honest, a healthy amount of nervousness. I still cannot believe that I am officially “Dr. Carter Bedinghaus.”

One of the greatest parts of residency has been getting to know my co-residents. It’s incredible how quickly a group of strangers can become a family. Having people who understand exactly what you are going through makes even the busiest days more rewarding. We have even started our own weekly tradition, “Aloha Friday,” where Hawaiian shirts are the unofficial uniform and we bring a little extra fun to the residency every Friday.

What has surprised me most is how different pediatric dentistry truly is.

Pediatric dentistry is about so much more than restoring teeth. Every appointment is an opportunity to build trust, create positive experiences, and shape how a child views dentistry for years to come. Sometimes, the greatest success is not the restoration; it’s a child leaving with a smile.

One of the most exciting parts of residency has been realizing how much there still is to learn. I’m gaining experience with restorative and surgical techniques, orthodontic appliances, and even the fundamentals of braces. Most importantly, I have had the opportunity to treat children with rare and medically complex conditions, including syndromes affecting as few as one in a million children. Every patient continues to challenge me to grow, think beyond the teeth, and become a better pediatric dentist.

Along with that excitement has come a whole new level of responsibility. “With great power comes great responsibility” may be one of the most recognizable movie quotes of all time, but residency has given those words an entirely new meaning.

As a student, there was always someone looking over my shoulder. Now, I’m learning what it truly means to be the doctor. Every diagnosis, treatment plan, and conversation with a parent carries a new level of responsibility, something that’s both exciting and humbling.

Residency quickly pushed me beyond my comfort zone. From treating children under general anesthesia to taking hospital calls and responding to emergencies, every experience has challenged me to think quickly, act confidently, and grow as a pediatric dentist.

Looking back, it’s incredible how much life has changed in just a few months. I graduated from dental school, stepped into opportunities I never expected—including filming for television—and began the rewarding challenge of pediatric residency. Through it all, I’ve been reminded that dentistry is so much more than a career. It has given me lifelong friendships, incredible mentors, and experiences I never could have imagined.

The road ahead will continue to challenge me, but that’s what excites me most. Looking back, I’m grateful for how far I’ve come, even more grateful for the people who helped me get here, and excited for everything that’s still ahead. When I graduated from dental school, I thought I had made it. Residency quickly reminded me that graduation wasn’t the finish line—it was the starting line. And honestly, I wouldn’t have it any other way.
